transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Hello, Doctor. Thank you so much for taking the time to see me, I really appreciate it. Um... I hope I'm not overreacting by being here, I just... I want to make sure I'm handling things correctly. Is it okay if I just explain what's been going on at work? 

I'm a translator, and... well, for a few months now, I've been seeing this pattern in our project files. I really don't want to sound like I'm throwing anyone under the bus, because I always try to be a team player, but... it looks like certain subcontractors and one of my colleagues keep making these tiny, tiny changes to the translation memory and the timestamps. It's just enough to make it look like my quality control failed. 

I even asked IT to look into it, and they told me the audit trail is completely clean. I know how that sounds, and I really don't want to seem difficult or paranoid, but I just know the record has been arranged somehow to put the blame on me. Does that make sense? I just want to figure out the right way to deal with all this so I can get back to doing good work.
Do you think someone is intentionally trying to sabotage your work?

Sabotage... gosh, that’s such a strong word, isn't it? I really hate to use it, because I don't want you to think I'm the kind of person who creates drama or points fingers. I always try to get along with everyone. 

But... well, yes, like I was just explaining, I do think it has to be intentional. The way those tiny changes are made to the translation memory by that colleague and the subcontractors—it's just too specific to be a simple accident. And even though IT told me the audit trail is completely clean, I... I just know the records have been arranged somehow to make it look like my quality control failed. 

I'm sorry, I know how paranoid that probably sounds to you. I really, really don't want to come across that way. Do you think I'm overreacting by looking at it like this?
How long have you been noticing these changes to the translation memory and timestamps?

Well, um... it's been about 11 months now. I think it started shortly after I was put in charge of the new localization project. 

I hope I don't sound like I've been holding onto a grudge for almost a year, because I really haven't. I just... I kept quiet about it for a long time because I didn't want to make a fuss or seem like I couldn't handle the responsibility of the new role. I kept telling myself maybe I was just tired or misinterpreting things. But it's just been going on for so long now. 

Is 11 months a long time to wait before talking to someone about this? I just wanted to be absolutely sure before I said anything that could cause trouble for anyone else.
Do you think these changes could have any other explanation besides someone intentionally trying to sabotage you?

I... well, I've really tried to think of other explanations. I promise you, I have. I don't want to think badly of my team, I really don't. I kept telling myself it was just a software glitch, or maybe a version control issue... but... 

I mean, I'm here today because for months now, I've just been seeing the exact same pattern in the project files. It's always those same certain subcontractors and that one colleague. They just keep making these tiny, tiny changes to the translation memory and the timestamps. And it always, always happens in a way that makes it look like my quality control failed. 

I know IT said the audit trail is clean, and I know how stubborn I must sound for not just accepting that. I'm sorry if I'm being difficult. But... I just know the record has been arranged somehow to put the blame on me. It's the only thing that makes sense of all the pieces. Does that make sense to you? I really hope you don't think I'm just being unreasonable.
Do you think your colleague and the subcontractors are working together against you?

Oh, gosh... working together... that makes it sound like some sort of... of conspiracy, doesn't it? I really hate to use words like that. I don't want you to think I'm the type of person who just accuses people of ganging up on me. I respect my coworkers, I really do. 

But... well, yes, like I was mentioning a moment ago, it’s really the only way to explain the pattern I've been seeing in the project files for months now. The way those certain subcontractors and that specific colleague operate... they almost have to be coordinating it. The tiny changes they keep making to the translation memory and the timestamps—they align too perfectly across the workflow. They both touch the files in a way that always, without fail, makes it look like my quality control was the problem. 

I know I already brought up the IT department, and I'm sorry to keep harping on it, but even when IT tells me the audit trail is completely clean... I just know they've worked together to arrange the records to put the blame on me. They must have helped each other cover their tracks. 

I feel terrible even saying this out loud, to be honest with you. Does it make me sound awful to think they might be collaborating like this? I really always try to see the best in my team, I promise I do.
Do you think you would still believe someone is sabotaging you even if you were shown proof that the changes were accidental?

I... I really want to say yes, that I would just believe the proof. I want to be the kind of person who can look at a simple explanation and... and just accept it. I hate being difficult, I really do. 

But... and I know I'm repeating myself, I'm so sorry to keep bringing it back to this... because of what I’ve been seeing for months in those project files, I think I would just worry that the 'proof' was part of the manipulation. The pattern is just too specific. Those tiny changes to the translation memory and the timestamps by that one colleague and those subcontractors... they always, always happen in a way that makes it look like my quality control failed. 

So even if someone showed me documentation that looked perfectly normal—like when IT told me the audit trail was clean—I... I just know the record has been arranged to put the blame on me. I wouldn't be able to just accept that it was an accident, because the pieces fit together too perfectly to be random. 

I know how stubborn that sounds. It makes me sound completely unreasonable, doesn't it? I really hope you don't think less of me for saying that. I just want to be completely honest with you.
How certain are you that someone is intentionally sabotaging your work?

I... gosh, I know I keep circling back to the exact same details, and I really appreciate your patience with me today. I don't want to sound like a broken record. But to answer your question... I am... I'm entirely certain. 

I really, really wish I wasn't. I'd love nothing more than to be completely wrong about all of this. But like I was saying before, when you look at those project files every single day for months, and you see those same tiny alterations in the translation memory... it just leaves no room for doubt in my mind. Even with IT insisting the audit trail is perfectly clean, I just... I know the record was arranged to make it look like my fault. 

I feel awful being so... so inflexible about it. I know it probably makes me look terribly stubborn to sit here and say I'm completely sure someone is doing this to me. Am I coming across as too defensive? I really don't mean to be, I just... I can't unsee what's happening. I really hope you can understand where I'm coming from.
Would anything be able to convince you that the changes to the project files were not intentional?

I... gosh, I really want to say yes. I want to be the kind of person who is open-minded and reasonable. I know how important it is to be flexible, and I really try my best to be that way in every part of my life. I don't want to be difficult, I promise.

But... I just don't think anything could convince me otherwise at this point. I'm so sorry if that's disappointing to hear. It's just... like I've been saying, for months I've been seeing this exact same pattern in the project files. It's those specific subcontractors and that one colleague, constantly making those tiny, precise changes to the translation memory and the timestamps. It always, always ends up looking like my quality control failed. 

And, well, even when IT looks at it and tells me the audit trail is completely clean... it doesn't change what I see. It just means the record has been arranged to put the blame on me. I know it sounds like I'm just refusing to listen, and I feel terrible about that. Does it make me seem terribly closed-minded? I really don't want you to think badly of me, I just... I can't ignore what's right in front of me, you know?
Is there anything that could happen or anything someone could tell you that would make you question your belief that someone is sabotaging your work?

I... I know I keep giving you the same answer, and I feel just awful about it. I really do. I want to be a good patient, and I want to say, "Yes, absolutely, if someone just explained it differently, I'd change my mind." I hate sounding so rigid. It’s just... 

When you sit there every day and you look at those project files... and you see those exact same subcontractors, and that one colleague, making those tiny little changes to the translation memory and the timestamps... it's just so clearly designed to make my quality control look like it failed. I’ve been looking at this for months. 

So if someone came to me and told me I was wrong... even if it was IT telling me again that the audit trail is completely clean... it wouldn't make me question it. Because I just know, deep down, that the record has been arranged to put the blame on me. 

I'm so sorry. I know that's not what you want to hear, and I know it probably makes me sound terribly difficult to work with. I really am trying to be cooperative, I promise. Do you... do you think I'm just being completely unreasonable? I really hope you aren't too frustrated with me.
Do you think you might be misinterpreting things due to stress or anxiety?

I... gosh, I really have thought about that. I mean, I know stress can do strange things to a person, and I definitely want to be open to that possibility. I really try to be self-aware, you know? I don't want to be the kind of person who just blindly ignores logic because they're a little overwhelmed at work. 

But... and I'm so sorry to keep coming back to this, I know I must sound like a broken record... it's just that the things I'm seeing aren't feelings, they're actual changes in the project files. It's those specific subcontractors, and that one colleague, and the tiny alterations to the translation memory and the timestamps. It's been going on for months, and it's always exactly the same pattern that makes it look like my quality control failed. 

Even if my anxiety was high, it wouldn't change the fact that IT says the audit trail is clean, which... well, it just confirms to me that the record was deliberately arranged to put the blame on me. 

I know it sounds like I'm just dismissing your suggestion, and I feel terrible about that. I really do appreciate you bringing it up. It's a very fair question. I just... I can't chalk this up to stress when the evidence is right there on my screen every day. Does that make sense? I really hope I don't sound too defensive about it.
Do you think you might be losing your grip on reality?

Oh, goodness, no. I mean, I really hope you don't think that. I know we've been talking about this a lot, and I know I must sound so... fixated. I worry so much that I'm coming across as crazy or irrational, and I really, really don't want you to see me that way. I pride myself on being a very grounded, professional person. 

But losing my grip on reality? No, I... I don't think so at all. Because everything I'm telling you is based on tangible things. It's not in my head, it's right there in the project files. I'm here because for months I've been seeing this exact same pattern. It's those certain subcontractors, and that one colleague, and they keep making these tiny, deliberate changes to the translation memory and the timestamps. It's all orchestrated so that it looks like my quality control failed. 

And I know we've talked about IT, and how they say the audit trail is clean. I know how that sounds to you, I really do. But to me, it just proves that the record has been arranged to put the blame on me. It's a very real, very concrete situation I'm dealing with at work. 

I'm so sorry, I feel like I'm frustrating you by repeating myself. I really want to be helpful and give you the answers you're looking for. Do you... do you think I sound like I'm losing touch with reality? I really hope I'm making at least a little bit of sense to you.
Do you think your concerns about sabotage could be a sign of a problem with your own thinking?

I... oh, I really hate having to push back on you again. I feel like I'm being such a difficult patient today, and I really, really don't want to be. I know the easiest thing would be to just agree with you and say, yes, it's a problem with my thinking. Honestly, part of me wishes it was just my thinking, because then maybe we could just fix it, right? 

But... and I'm so sorry to bring it right back to this... it's just that I can't ignore what I'm looking at. I've been seeing this same pattern in the project files for months now. It's not an imagination thing. It's those specific subcontractors, and that one colleague, and they keep making these tiny, exact changes to the translation memory and the timestamps. It's all set up so it looks like my quality control failed. 

I know you keep trying to help me see it from another angle, especially since IT said the audit trail is clean. I know that makes my story sound so... unbelievable. I'm so embarrassed even talking about it because I know how it sounds. But to me, that clean audit trail just means the record has been carefully arranged to put the blame on me. 

I promise I'm not trying to be stubborn or dismissive of your expertise. You're the doctor, and I have so much respect for you. It's just... how do I say it's my thinking when the files are right there on my screen? Am I making this incredibly frustrating for you? I really want to do this right, I just don't know how to unsee what they're doing to my work.
Have you ever had similar concerns about people plotting against you in the past?

No, no, never. Gosh, I really hope I'm not giving you the impression that I'm just... naturally suspicious of people or something. I've always gotten along really well with my colleagues in the past. I pride myself on being a team player, you know? 

I've never had any issues like this before. That's why this whole situation is so distressing for me. I'm usually the person who gives everyone the benefit of the doubt. I've never thought anyone was out to get me or plotting anything in any of my previous jobs. 

I just... I really want you to know that this isn't how I usually am. It's just this one specific situation with these specific files and this one colleague. Does that help clarify things? I really want to make sure I'm giving you the right picture of who I am.
Have you ever suspected that someone was sabotaging you outside of work?

Oh, um, no. Definitely not. I really hope it doesn't seem like I'm just... suspicious of everyone everywhere. My personal life is actually very quiet, very normal. I have great relationships with my friends and family. 

I really don't want you to think I'm walking around looking over my shoulder at the grocery store or anything like that! I know how concerning that would be, and I promise that's not me at all. It's really just... strictly limited to those project files at the office. 

Does that make sense? I really want to assure you that outside of this one very specific work issue, everything else in my life is completely fine. I hope that's a good sign, right?
Have you ever had a period of time where you didn't think someone was sabotaging your work?

Well, before this current project, yes, absolutely. I never had any worries like this at all. Everything was completely fine until... gosh, it's been about 11 months now. 

It started shortly after I was put in charge of the new localization project. Before that, I never had a single concern about my work being tampered with. I really hope that shows that I'm not just someone who always thinks the worst of people. It's really just been this past year, with this specific project. Is that the kind of timeline you were looking for? I want to make sure I'm answering your questions properly.
Have you ever had a period where you doubted your belief that someone is sabotaging your work?

I really, really tried to. I wanted to be wrong, I honestly did. I don't want to be the kind of person who points fingers or creates drama. I kept telling myself, you know, maybe I'm just overthinking it, maybe it's just a system glitch. 

But... well, honestly, I’m here because for months now, I’ve been seeing the exact same pattern in the project files. It's just so clear to me. Certain subcontractors and that one colleague keep making these tiny, tiny changes to the translation memory and the timestamps. It's done in a very specific way so it looks like my quality control failed. 

I know how this might sound to you, and I really don't want to come across as difficult or paranoid. I even had IT look at it, genuinely hoping they'd just tell me I was making a mistake and put my mind at ease. And... well, IT did say the audit trail is clean. I know I should probably just smile and accept that, but... I just know the record has been arranged to put the blame on me. The edits are just too precise. 

I really hope you don't think I'm just being stubborn or irrational by not letting it go. I just take my job very seriously, and it's hard to ignore what's right in front of me. Does it make sense why I'd have such a hard time doubting it, given all those patterns? I just want to make sure I'm explaining it clearly.
Do you think there's any possibility, no matter how small, that you might be mistaken about someone sabotaging your work?

I... I really want to say yes. I want to be the kind of person who can step back and say, 'Okay, I'm just stressed, I'm making a mistake.' And I know that's probably what you're hoping to hear, right? That I have some insight into this and I'm not just completely stuck in my own head. 

But... well, I've just been looking at these project files for months. And the pattern is just... it's right there. The subcontractors and that one colleague, they're making these tiny, tiny alterations to the translation memory and the timestamps. It's so specific, so perfectly designed to make it look like my quality control is failing. 

I know IT said the audit trail is clean. I know how that sounds, and I'm really sorry if it makes me seem difficult or... or detached from reality. I really don't want to come across that way. It's just that I know the record has been arranged to put the blame on me. The edits are just too precise to be accidental. 

I really hope you can understand where I'm coming from. I'm not trying to be combative, I promise. It's just... when you see the same pattern over and over, it's hard to just pretend it's not happening. Does that make sense? I hope I'm not disappointing you by saying that.
Do you think there is any evidence that could change your mind about someone sabotaging your work?

I... gosh, I really wish I could give you a simple 'yes.' I'd love nothing more than for someone to show me something that just... makes it all go away. I want to be a reasonable person, I really do. 

But, like I was mentioning a minute ago about the IT department... they did show me what should have been evidence. They showed me the clean audit trail. And I know most people would just accept that, and I promise you, I really tried to. I didn't want to cause a fuss or seem uncooperative with them. 

It's just... because of my background, I know exactly how translation memory works. So when I see that the record itself has been carefully arranged to put the blame on me... well, if the evidence—the timestamps, the logs—if that's exactly what's being manipulated by them, then I just don't know what kind of proof could actually uncover the truth. 

I'm so sorry, I know that probably sounds like I'm just being impossible or closed-minded. I really don't want to be that kind of person for you. Am I making any sense at all? I just want to make sure I'm answering your questions the right way.
Have you ever had a moment where you didn't believe someone was sabotaging your work at all?

I... well, I guess before all this started, of course. I just went to work, did my translations, and came home. I want to say that there are days now where I just wake up and think, 'Oh, it's all fine, I'm just imagining it.' I really try to have those moments. 

But... I'm so sorry, I feel like I'm repeating myself and I don't want to bore you or seem like a broken record. It's just... for months now, I've been looking at these project files. And it's not a feeling, it's a pattern. I see the subcontractors and that one colleague making these tiny, tiny changes to the translation memory and the timestamps. It's done so specifically to make it look like my quality control failed. 

And I know we talked about the IT department, and I know they said the audit trail is clean. I really wish I could just nod and agree with them, I really do. But I just know that the record itself has been arranged to put the blame on me. 

I'm sorry, I know that's not the answer you were hoping for. I really want to be cooperative and give you the right answers. Am I just being too difficult about this? I hope you can see that I'm really trying to look at this objectively, even if it doesn't sound like it.
